newsitem.title: POLAND: Espebepe to accept creditor's offer.
newsitem.headline: Espebepe to accept creditor's offer.

text.p: Polish construction company Espebepe SA said it would accept its largest creditor's debt-restructuring plan if creditors agree to its conditions on financing the scheme, the firm said in a statement.

Espebepe said in a Wednesday statement that it had sent a letter to its largest creditor, Pomorski Bank Kredytowy SA (PBKS), saying it would accept PBKS' proposal to write off 40 percent of its debts and to change the remaining into convertible bonds.

"To conclude the deal on conditions set by PBKS it is necessary to have assurance from PBKS or other creditor banks of financial assurance to execute the conditions of the deal," Espebepe said without giving details.
"The company must have sources of financing after the deal is concluded for its creditors who would not be interested in buying the bonds or converting them into shares," it said.
No one at the firm was immediately available for comment.
On Tuesday Espebepe's president told Reuters that PBKS's proposal could be implemented if the bank would underwrite the issue.

Espebepe earlier said it wanted its largest creditors to write off 95 percent of its 75-million-zloty debt and then to raise the firm's capital by taking over a new share issue at five zlotys per share.
A creditors meeting is scheduled for May 16 after two previous ones on March 14 and April 14 failed to decide the fate of the firm.
Espebepe has said the May meeting would be the last one at which a decision on a debt-deal or bankruptcy must be taken.
